name: REN-related Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease
aliases: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease due to REN mutations

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic REN gene mutation by genetic testing
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease with anemia and hyperuricemia
Renal biopsy showing tubulointerstitial fibrosis with minimal glomerular involvement
Exclusion of other causes of tubulointerstitial kidney disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic REN mutation plus compatible clinical features and family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; renal biopsy is supportive but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Often precedes decline in kidney function
searchTerms: normal size red blood cells anemia
low red blood cells without color change

pathognomonic.notes: May present in adolescence or early adulthood
searchTerms: high uric acid with gout attacks

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive tubulointerstitial nephropathy leading to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: chronic kidney disease from tubulointerstitial nephropathy

common.symptomName: Polyuria and polydipsia due to impaired concentrating ability
Fatigue related to anemia and renal insufficiency
searchTerms: tiredness from anemia and kidney problems
fatigue due to low red blood cells and kidney issues
weakness related to anemia and kidney failure

laboratory: Normocytic normochromic anemia with low erythropoietin levels
Hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis in advanced disease
imaging: Renal ultrasound typically normal or shows small kidneys with increased echogenicity
Occasional renal cysts in late stages
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Renal biopsy showing tubulointerstitial fibrosis with minimal glomerular involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Mutation in MUC1 gene instead of REN
Absence of early anemia and hyperuricemia
Presence of medullary cysts on imaging

redFlags: Family history of progressive kidney disease with autosomal dominant pattern
Hyperuricemia with gout in young patients
references: Bleyer AJ et al. Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: diagnosis, classification, and management. Kidney Int. 2017.
Olinger E et al. REN mutations cause autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease. Kidney Int. 2016.
Orphanet Report: REN-related autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease. Orphanet 2023.
